product_from_film: Clear Signing is presented as a standard for making Ethereum transaction-signing details readable to people.
explains_well: An opening question about what a user is signing is followed by captioned contributors explaining the purpose and adoption need.
unclear: No actual before-and-after wallet signing screen or completed user decision is shown.
scenario: Explain unreadable signing requests, the proposed readable alternative, ecosystem adoption and remaining security limits.
product_clear_basis: Opening text names ERC-7730 and making Ethereum human-readable around 10–13s; contributor captions repeat the purpose later.

categories.finding: Opaque signing problem → named standard → contributor explanations → risk and adoption → limitation → title.
Cables and numeric blocks create a technical opening; the user problem is not explicit in the first two seconds.
Readable transaction signing is described around 12s. Wallet users and ecosystem implementers are implied, but their actual steps are not shown.
Opening text changes position as more lines appear; the main body uses ordinary talking-head gestures. No detailed interface motion is demonstrated.
Changes of speaker create most scene changes after 20s. Repeated frames, labels and captions keep the format stable.
Grain-like colored borders and old-display opening contrast with varied home/office webcam backgrounds.
Opening monospaced paragraphs require sustained reading. Bottom captions carry most of the long explanation; the final title is much larger.
Captioned interview content and ASR describe the standard and adoption. Actual pace, clarity, accents and delivery are unverified without listening.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Webcam-style contributor recordings are placed in a shared graphic frame; capture setup and asset provenance are unknown.
Source duration 166.449 s; Watch metadata 1440 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: Captions make the conceptual explanation available silently, but the viewer never sees a concrete improved signing request.
Faces occupy the center while names sit above and subtitles below; sustained reading competes with watching each speaker.
Several speakers repeat readability and risk points across over two minutes. A real example could replace some repetition.
The opening What am I actually signing question receives verbal explanation, but no visual before/after answer.
Warning-like imagery and risk testimony may create concern, followed by reassurance and a closing limit; viewer effect is unmeasured.
Shared colored frame and caption placement unify contributors with different backgrounds.

The film states availability, implementation and security claims. No wallet behavior, adoption coverage or loss-prevention effect is independently verified. The final speaker explicitly limits the promise.
Ethereum symbol, contributor labels and standard number make the topic specific, despite a common interview format.
A side-by-side unreadable request and readable request would explain the core change more directly than another interview statement.
categories.experiment: Replace one repeated explanation with the same transaction shown in both signing formats.

categories.finding: For Tin, explain a complex trust feature with one real decision screen and a clear before/after.
categories.experiment: Show an unclear approval request beside one with exact asset, channel, date and action details.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Use a consistent frame and caption system to join many contributor recordings, and retain a clear limit on the promise.
try: Replace one repeated interview point with the same transaction shown as an unreadable request and a clear request.
For Tin, compare an unclear approval request with one showing the exact asset, destination, date and action.
lessons.avoid: Letting expert testimony and availability labels substitute for a concrete user-facing example.
lessons.open: Standard implementation details, adoption coverage, wallet behavior, security outcomes, source identities and audio remain unverified.
